corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies on large language models, the corpus reveals converging concerns about how AI is adopted in organizations and households, how LLMs serve as research tools, how AI affects health information and wellbeing, and how ethics, fairness, and trust influence human-AI interaction. The records emphasize evaluation frameworks, governance, and education-focused responses.

themes.name: AI adoption and social dynamics
themes.description: Studies examine how individuals, organizations, and communities adopt generative AI, how peer effects, trust, and social norms shape use, and how governance and policy contexts respond.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and methodological innovation
themes.description: Papers show LLMs enabling data extraction, codebook creation, cross-domain analysis, simulations, and governance studies while highlighting validation, transparency, and ethical considerations.

themes.name: AI in health, education, and wellbeing
themes.description: Research investigates AI-driven health information, education technologies, counseling, and wellbeing outcomes, including misinformation risks and user trust.

themes.name: Fairness, safety, and human-centered AI design
themes.description: A thread across papers on bias, fairness, safety, perceived humanness, and design frameworks (e.g., Value-Sensitive Design, ADE) to ground AI in human values.

emergingKeywords: perceived humanness and empathy in AI
ethics and bias in AI systems
